hypothesis_update: Leading data-integrity/correctness hypothesis: lower_compose mis-lowers init statements because the alias-visible set is inconsistent across the two init paths — component inits get an empty set (rewrite_statements(..., &HashSet::new())) while compose inits get the full components map (rewrite_compose_statements(..., &components)). If that argument is the set of resolvable aliases, references inside a component's own init would silently fail to resolve or be mis-substituted, producing a KernelSpec with dangling references. Secondary suspicion: the internal action-filter set (lines 291-298) excludes actions without validating that the referenced alias+action exists, contradicting the documented contract that unknown aliases/actions return CoreError. statement-rewrite will confirm whether the empty-set path is a real resolution bug or by-design component self-containment.
rationale: The received target body (compose.rs:249-372) shows a concrete asymmetry: component-level SpecItem::Init is lowered via rewrite_statements(statements.clone(), component, &HashSet::new()) (~line 315) with an empty set, while compose-level Common(Init) uses rewrite_compose_statements(statements.clone(), &components) (~line 345) with the full component map. The statement-rewrite card (585-740) contains exactly these two functions, so it reveals what that third argument means and how it is consumed, i.e. whether the empty set leaves aliases inside a component's own init unresolved. It is also the largest card, indicating the densest core logic.
